claim: Ferrari Dacrema et al. find that 6 of 18 reproduced neural recommender-system papers can be outperformed by simple heuristic (nearest-neighbor or graph-based) methods, and only 1 of the 18 clearly outperformed baselines without also losing to a well-tuned non-neural linear ranking method.
stance_target: the 'audits shrink' pattern generally cited alongside melis2018sota
scope_conditions: 18 neural recommendation papers from KDD, SIGIR, WWW, RecSys (2015-2018)
quoted_support: "it turned out that 6 of them can often be outperformed with comparably simple heuristic methods, e.g., based on nearest-neighbor or graph-based techniques. The remaining one clearly outperformed the baselines but did not consistently outperform a well-tuned non-neural linear ranking method."

claim: A traditional ItemKNN method, when properly configured, outperforms the neural MCRec model on all measured performance metrics.
stance_target: specific case-study evidence for the shrink direction
quoted_support: "Table 3 shows that the traditional ItemKNN method, when configured correctly, outperforms MCRec on all performance measures."

claim: SpectralCF, a neural graph-based recommender, performed worse than baseline methods in every configuration tested and was even outperformed by a non-personalized TopPopular baseline.
stance_target: specific case-study evidence for the shrink direction
scope_conditions: SpectralCF reproduction case study, multiple datasets
quoted_support: "SpectralCF in all configurations performed worse than our baseline methods and was outperformed even by the TopPopular method."
